questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me that there was beautiful nature around, and that it was a cute city, not necessarily a big one.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, and if I was in doubt I knew who to write an email to. Once you get there you will be familiar with the international office.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an introduction day for international students where we got a lot of useful information. And we got a lot of emails from them as well. Students of UCC also gave us a tour of the campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It's hard to find accommodation in Cork, because there is a housing crisis. There is a lot of private student accommodations though, and I think this is the best way to go about it. There is also a lot of private people who rent out rooms in Cork, but then you usually have less freedom to bring friends over and make the space your own.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's gonna be expensive and hard to find accommodation, but it's worth it. I lived at Brookfield on college road and it was 5 minutes away from UCC. I was super happy with my place.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to get registered at UCC. There was a lot of steps. But they sent tutorials, videos and clear instructions on how to do it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Tutorials, videos and clear instructions sent by the international office. Fear not, there is help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Most of courses I looked at from home was not the ones I ended up taking. Either because UCC didn't have them anymore or I found others more interesting. But the ones I wanted and registered for, I ended up getting.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't get too set on the courses you choose at home. There will probably be changes in the program.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The levels are different from course to course and from field to field. Generally it isn't a high level. The classes are not as analytical as the ones at University of Copenhagen. And there is not as much reading. But there is more assignments to do.
The first year classes are really easy, and generally the music classes I took was a pretty low level. My film courses however were really good and challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Most of the time it is lectures where the teacher talks and then prompts the students to discuss about something in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Singers and Songs in Irish tradition
Case studies in European Cinema
American Cinema: Hollywood and beyond 1953-1973
Western Music, Culture and Media
Music in Culture and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Case studies in European Cinema
American Cinema: Hollywood and beyond 1953-1973

These were my favourite classes and the teachers at the film study faculty are so nice and knowledgable.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I bought a bike there which was pretty pricey. I wouldn't recommend it. Cork is small enough to walk around in.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Beer is actually more expensive than I anticipated. I thought the beer in Ireland would be cheap, but it's the same prices as in Copenhagen. A normal pint is around 4-6 euro.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a loooot of clubs and societies to be a part of. The list is long. I never had the time to join any but if I could do my semester again I would prioritise doing it!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The mountaineering club. They make a lot of cheap hiking trips around Ireland. It's the perfect way to get out and see the beautiful nature.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Ballycotton Cliff Hike.
Dingle.
Dublin.
Killarney National Park.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
People are very nice so it was easy to adjust. Ireland has a very friendly culture in general.
The students are a bit different from students in Copenhagen. They all look the same, wear a lot of make up, sports clothes at uni and then very dolled up when they go out. All the boys wear jogging pants.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Talk to them in class they are very friendly.
Go to bars in the city on Thursdays, that's when all the local students go out before they go home to their families in the weekend.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way they dress up, which also tells something about their view on gender roles and norms. It's very gendered. The girls are very pretty, dolled up and has to care a lot about their appearance. The same isn't expected about the boys.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The drinking culture and the banter/friendliness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Pack good rain clothes
2. and sturdy hiking boots if you wanna hike. They should be rain proof
3. You are gonna spend more money on beer and going out than you anticipate

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Bring an extension cord.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: When me and my friends rented a cabin in the mountains<3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling burnt out in the beginning after doing so much and getting to know so many new people. Remember to take time for yourself and go explore on your own<3

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
